content:
Petra Zlatarić-Novosel
Osijek, Croatia | petra.zlataric@example.com | +385 55 555 0606 | github.com/pzn-ml-example

Dear Quillstone Payments Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. I bring more than five years of experience in NLP and document classification, with hands-on work taking machine-learning models from research and prototyping into production. Quillstone’s focus on helping merchants get support quickly through practical AI tools makes this role especially compelling to me.

In my current role at Slavonica Document AI, I developed an automated document-classification model that achieved 94% accuracy across 23 classes for public-sector clients. I have also fine-tuned BERTić and XLM-R for named entity recognition in Croatian documents, and deployed models as FastAPI services in Docker on Azure ML and Azure App Service. To support reliable operations, I introduced MLflow for experiment tracking and model registry and established production monitoring for data drift with weekly reporting. This experience aligns closely with your need to build, serve and monitor AI systems in production.

My earlier work includes building text-classification models for customer complaints using TF-IDF, logistic regression and fastText, as well as developing churn-prediction models with gradient boosting and LightGBM. Alongside my production experience, my PhD research on named entity recognition in Croatian legal texts has strengthened my ability to prepare and work with text data. I would welcome the opportunity to bring this combination of applied NLP, cloud deployment and production monitoring to Quillstone’s customer-support AI team and contribute to systems that help merchants and support agents.

Thank you for considering my application. I would be glad to discuss how my experience could contribute to Quillstone Payments.

Sincerely,
Petra Zlatarić-Novosel

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, concise, professional, and well structured. It uses specific evidence such as 94% accuracy across 23 classes, BERTić and XLM-R fine-tuning, FastAPI, Docker, Azure, MLflow, and production drift monitoring. The progression from current production work to earlier NLP and predictive-modelling experience is logical. However, it reads somewhat generically in places and does not address several important requirements explicitly, including the computer science degree, Python, MLOps terminology, or the candidate’s publication. It also does not connect the candidate’s experience as directly as it could to merchant support, ticket routing, support-agent tooling, or language-model evaluation.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly in plain text: standard headings and paragraphs, no problematic tables, graphics, columns, or unusual formatting. It includes useful keywords such as NLP, document classification, production, FastAPI, Docker, Azure ML, Azure App Service, MLflow, model registry, monitoring, data drift, TF-IDF, logistic regression, fastText, LightGBM, and text data. AI screening probability is moderate to good when evaluated with the associated CV, but weaker for the cover letter alone because it omits exact terms supported by the candidate’s information, especially Python, computer science, model versioning, and MLOps. It does not—and should not—add unsupported chat-assistant, RAG, feature-engineering, or data-ingestion claims.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the production ML, NLP, model-serving, monitoring, Azure, and MLflow aspects of the role. The candidate’s experience with text classification, customer complaint analysis, and production deployment is relevant to customer-support AI. The MSc in Computer Science and strong Python experience are present in the associated CV but not surfaced in the letter. The candidate’s material does not show experience with chat assistants or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), feature engineering, or data-ingestion pipelines. The source material also does not clearly establish at least four years specifically as a Machine Learning Engineer shipping systems to production; it shows an ML Engineer role from 2023 onward and earlier Data Scientist and research roles. These are job-alignment gaps rather than defects that can be repaired through wording. The letter also gives limited evidence of the company’s stated ownership, teamwork, pragmatism, learning, or candid-feedback culture.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL: In the second paragraph, after the opening sentence about production ML experience, explicitly mention the supported qualification: “I hold an MSc in Computer Science from Drava University and am currently pursuing PhD studies in Computer Science.” This makes the degree requirement visible in the cover letter.

CRITICAL: In the second paragraph, after describing FastAPI and Docker deployment, add the supported programming and MLOps terms: “Using Python, I have applied MLOps practices with MLflow for experiment tracking, model versioning and registry, and production monitoring.” Keep the existing Azure and deployment details, but use “model versioning” only in connection with the documented MLflow model registry experience.

MINOR: In the final body paragraph, make the customer-support relevance more specific without claiming unsupported experience. Change the sentence beginning “I would welcome the opportunity...” to: “I would welcome the opportunity to apply this combination of Python-based NLP, text classification, cloud deployment and production monitoring to AI systems that help support teams process and route merchant questions efficiently.” This connects the documented experience to the role without claiming experience with chat assistants or RAG.

MINOR: In the opening paragraph, replace the generic sentence “Quillstone’s focus on helping merchants get support quickly through practical AI tools makes this role especially compelling to me” with a more role-specific version such as: “The opportunity to build and operate practical AI systems for merchant support—working from prototype through production—particularly interests me.” This is more closely aligned with the advert while avoiding unsupported claims about the candidate’s prior use of chat assistants or RAG.

content:
Petra Zlatarić-Novosel

Dear Quillstone Payments Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. I bring more than five years of experience in NLP and document classification, with hands-on work taking machine-learning models from research and prototyping into production. The opportunity to build and operate practical AI systems for merchant support—working from prototype through production—particularly interests me.

In my current role at Slavonica Document AI, I developed an automated document-classification model that achieved 94% accuracy across 23 classes for public-sector clients. I hold an MSc in Computer Science from Drava University and am currently pursuing PhD studies in Computer Science. I have also fine-tuned BERTić and XLM-R for named entity recognition in Croatian documents, and deployed models as FastAPI services in Docker on Azure ML and Azure App Service. Using Python, I have applied MLOps practices with MLflow for experiment tracking, model versioning and registry, and production monitoring. To support reliable operations, I introduced MLflow for experiment tracking and model registry and established production monitoring for data drift with weekly reporting. This experience aligns closely with your need to build, serve and monitor AI systems in production.

My earlier work includes building text-classification models for customer complaints using TF-IDF, logistic regression and fastText, as well as developing churn-prediction models with gradient boosting and LightGBM. Alongside my production experience, my PhD research on named entity recognition in Croatian legal texts has strengthened my ability to prepare and work with text data. I would welcome the opportunity to apply this combination of Python-based NLP, text classification, cloud deployment and production monitoring to AI systems that help support teams process and route merchant questions efficiently.

Thank you for considering my application. I would be glad to discuss how my experience could contribute to Quillstone Payments.

Sincerely,
Petra Zlatarić-Novosel

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is professional, clear, and well structured. It presents relevant evidence from the candidate’s current and previous roles, including a measurable 94% classification result, transformer fine-tuning, FastAPI deployment, Azure, MLflow, and production monitoring. The connection to building, serving, and monitoring production AI systems is credible. The main content weakness is repetition: MLflow experiment tracking and model registry are mentioned twice in the same paragraph. The letter also gives limited evidence of collaboration, ownership, or operational responsibility beyond mentoring two students, although the available candidate information does not support stronger claims.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document uses a simple, ATS-friendly structure with standard headings, readable text, and no problematic tables, graphics, or unusual formatting. It includes strong searchable terms such as Python, NLP, text classification, model serving, FastAPI, Docker, Azure ML, Azure App Service, MLflow, model registry, monitoring, data drift, and production. AI screening probability is moderate to high for the supported requirements, but likely reduced because the letter does not contain supported evidence for chat assistants or RAG, feature engineering, or data ingestion pipelines. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than wording defects, so they should not be added without evidence.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with the production ML aspects of the role: the candidate has a computer science degree, production model deployment, Azure experience, Python, MLflow, model serving, and data-drift monitoring. The NLP and text-classification background is relevant to customer-support automation and ticket routing. However, the candidate’s material does not show experience with AI products such as chat assistants or RAG, four years specifically as a Machine Learning Engineer shipping production systems, feature engineering, or data ingestion pipelines. These are genuine profile gaps, not defects that can be fixed through rewriting. The letter also does not demonstrate direct experience with merchant-support systems, but it appropriately avoids claiming such experience.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL: In the second paragraph, remove the repeated sentence beginning "To support reliable operations, I introduced MLflow..." because the preceding sentence already states that MLflow was used for experiment tracking and the model registry. Retain one concise version, for example: "Using Python, I applied MLOps practices with MLflow for experiment tracking and model registry, and established production monitoring for data drift with weekly reporting." This will improve concision and eliminate redundancy.

MINOR: In the second paragraph, replace "model versioning and registry" with the more precise, directly supported phrase "model registry." The original candidate information explicitly supports MLflow for experiment tracking and a model registry, but does not separately state data or model versioning practices. A precise sentence would be: "Using Python, I applied MLOps practices with MLflow for experiment tracking and model registry, and established production monitoring for data drift with weekly reporting."
